sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year from $1.70 billion in FY2016 to $12.0 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].

The step change came in FY2020, when revenue rose 49.1% to $6.21 billion on the U.S. launch of TRIKAFTA in the fourth quarter of 2019 and KAFTRIO in the EU in the third quarter of 2020 [F5][D194][P51].
FY2024 broke the pattern with a $233 million operating loss and a $536 million net loss, driven by $4.4 billion of non-deductible acquired IPR&D from the Alpine acquisition [F24][F44][P5].
Growth has decelerated since: revenue rose 10.5% in FY2023, 11.7% in FY2024 and 8.9% in FY2025, and the three-year CAGR to FY2025 was 10.4% [D352][D402][D446][D679].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO was the engine, contributing 29.5pp of FY2021 growth and 26.3pp in FY2022, and still 85.9% of FY2025 revenue [D519][D522][D529].
In FY2025 net product revenues rose $950.5 million, or 9%, primarily due to continued growth, with ALYFTREK adding 7.6pp and TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO only 0.7pp [P3][D590][D531].
Operating costs fell 30.4% in FY2025 while revenue grew 8.9%, so revenue growth exceeded operating-cost growth by 39.3pp, at operating-cost growth of -30.4% [D457][D446][D464].
Diluted EPS rose from $13.89 in FY2023 to $15.32 in FY2025 while the diluted share count was flat at 258.0 million, so per-share growth tracked net income [F73][F75][X137][D459].
The FY2025 operating margin of 34.8% sat above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% FY2022 high, and well above the -2.1% FY2024 low [F35][D663][D662][D661].
The FY2025 margin recovery of 36.9pp came mostly from the residual line at +37.7pp, with R&D +0.4pp, cost of revenue +0.1pp and SG&A -1.3pp [D452][D468][D466][D465][D467].
Cost of sales held at 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 as a result of a lower overall royalty rate for the CF medicines [D425][P4].
In FY2025 net margin of 32.9% sat 1.8pp below the 34.8% operating margin, a gap of -1.8pp [F55][F35][D708].
Operating cash flow was $3.63 billion in FY2025, primarily due to income from operations of $4.17 billion [F85][F25][P1].
That was 0.92x net income, below the 1.16x window median, and free cash flow of $3.19 billion was 0.81x net income against a 1.07x median [D434][D698][F105][D435][D675].
Free cash flow margin was 26.6%, below the 32.8% window median and the 48.2% FY2020 high [D431][D669][D668].
Capex of $438 million was 3.6% of revenue and 2.09x D&A, up from 1.44x in FY2024 [F95][D430][D436][D391].
Cash and investments were $12.3 billion at FY2025, net cash of $12.3 billion and 102.7% of revenue, with no debt [D438][D439][D440][D13].
That net cash position ranked in the 88th percentile of eight biopharma peers against a -50.7% peer median [D691][D692].
Cash rose 9.8% in FY2025 primarily due to increased cash and marketable securities from product revenue [D460][P2].
Buybacks of $2.02 billion absorbed 63.2% of free cash flow in FY2025, up from 12.8% in FY2023, while the diluted share count was unchanged [D441][D442][D348][D459].
Days inventory outstanding rose 85 days to 373 days in FY2025, from 287 days in FY2024, with inventory up 39.9% against revenue growth of 8.9% [D444][D397][D462][D446].
Inventory is building far faster than sales, which ties up cash and raises the risk of write-downs if demand shifts [R1].
The effective tax rate moved -300.7pp in FY2025 to 14.9% from 315.5% in FY2024 [D433][D390].
The FY2024 rate was distorted by the non-deductible Alpine IPR&D, so the FY2025 rate is the cleaner baseline and the swing is largely benign [R2][P5].
Whether TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth recovers above the 0.7% FY2025 rate or ALYFTREK's 7.6pp contribution holds, in the FY2026 10-K [D530][D590].
Whether days inventory outstanding falls back toward the 287 days of FY2024 or stays above the 373 days of FY2025, in the FY2026 10-K [D397][D444].
Whether the operating margin holds above the 31.8% window median or slips toward the -2.1% FY2024 low, in the FY2026 10-K [D663][D661].
